title: Remidio with RetinaRisk to Strengthen AI-Driven Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in India and Iceland
summary: Remidio and Iceland-based RetinaRisk announced a partnership to expand AI-driven diabetic retinopathy screening across India and Iceland. The collaboration will integrate RetinaRisk's cloud-based risk and detection algorithms with Remidio's retinal imaging devices to improve early detection, support teleophthalmology, and increase access to screening in urban and rural clinics through pilots, clinician training and regulatory-aligned validation.
content:
Remidio, an Indian medical technology company known for compact retinal imaging devices, has partnered with Icelandic AI health firm RetinaRisk to expand AI-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening programs in India and Iceland. The collaboration aims to combine Remidio's field-proven fundus cameras with RetinaRisk's cloud-based AI analytics to accelerate early detection and treatment referrals for people with diabetes.

Remidio's handheld and clinic-grade non-mydriatic cameras are designed for screening in primary-care settings and remote outreach camps. The company has focused on affordability and portability to reach underserved populations in India, and has partnered with public and private health programs to scale retinal imaging in community clinics and diabetes centers.

RetinaRisk brings validated machine-learning models and a risk-scoring platform that assess an individual's likelihood of diabetic eye disease progression. Its technology supports automated analysis of retinal images, longitudinal risk tracking and integration with telemedicine workflows. RetinaRisk has emphasized clinical validation and regulatory compliance in European markets and aims to adapt its algorithms for diverse populations.

Under the agreement, the partners will integrate RetinaRisk's analysis pipeline with Remidio's imaging systems and cloud infrastructure. The integrated solution will enable instant image upload, automated DR detection and risk stratification, and prioritized referral suggestions for ophthalmology follow-up. Initial deployments will include pilot programs in urban diabetes clinics and rural screening camps in India, alongside targeted implementations in Iceland to refine performance across different populations.

The collaboration includes clinician training, workflow integration, and prospective validation studies to measure diagnostic accuracy and operational impact. Data privacy and local regulatory requirements will be addressed through anonymized data handling, secure cloud services, and adherence to regional health data standards. The partners expect the solution to reduce screening bottlenecks, shorten time to referral, and lower the number of preventable vision loss cases through earlier intervention.

"Combining Remidio's imaging reach with RetinaRisk's AI analytics creates a practical path to scalable, high-quality screening," said a Remidio spokesperson. "Our goal is to make diabetic eye screening routine and accessible beyond tertiary centers." A RetinaRisk representative added, "We are focused on delivering clinically robust risk tools that integrate into existing care pathways and support clinicians in prioritizing patients at highest risk."

Both companies outlined plans for phased rollouts accompanied by peer-reviewed validation and engagement with health authorities. If pilots demonstrate improved detection rates and cost-effectiveness, the partners plan broader adoption across public health programs, private clinics and teleophthalmology networks. The initiative is positioned as part of a wider effort to use AI and affordable imaging technology to close gaps in diabetic eye care and prevent avoidable blindness.

Observers note that success will depend on implementation at scale, clinician acceptance, and ensuring AI models perform reliably across diverse ethnic and socioeconomic groups. The Remidio-RetinaRisk partnership aims to address these challenges through local validation, clinician training, and iterative model tuning based on real-world data.
